resources.string: Click a phone number in your computer\'s browser and this phone opens its dialer with the number ready. Generate a pairing code below and paste it into the browser extension.
The app keeps its own connection open. Nothing Google-owned is involved, and it works on phones without Play Services. Costs a little battery.
Borrows the connection Google Play Services already maintains, so it costs almost no battery. Google routes the message, but the number inside it is encrypted and unreadable to them.
Firebase is not available in this build. Rebuild with a google-services.json, or use the app\'s own connection.
Android may stop the app to save power. Exempting it keeps calls arriving reliably.
This app stores a server address, a topic name, an encryption key and a Firebase token. It never stores the numbers you are sent, and sends nothing to anyone but the delivery service you chose.
Waiting for pushes via Google Play Services
Shown when your computer sends a number to this phone
The quiet notice that the app is listening
Paste this into the browser extension. It contains your encryption key, so treat it like a password.
Fill in the settings above, then generate again.
Everything stored by this app has been deleted.
This removes the pairing, the encryption key and all settings. Your browser will no longer be able to reach this phone until you pair again.
